report.tagline: A paid AI tool that turns a short text description into striking, art-quality images and short videos.
report.simpleSummary: You type what you want to see, like 'a tiger in a Mumbai street at sunset, oil painting', and Midjourney makes four images in seconds. You pick one, tweak it, and download it. It started inside Discord, a chat app, and now also has its own website. It has no free plan, about 40 staff, no outside investors, and still makes hundreds of millions of dollars a year.

keyNumbers.label: Annual revenue run rate
keyNumbers.note: Analyst estimate. Midjourney does not publish numbers. The Disney lawsuit said $300M for the prior year (2024).

keyNumbers.label: Employees
keyNumbers.note: Multiple reports, 2026. That is roughly $12M of revenue per person.

keyNumbers.label: Outside funding
keyNumbers.note: Founder David Holz has turned down venture capital. Profitable within about six months of public launch in 2022.

keyNumbers.note: Estimate from public Discord server counts; not all are paying or active.

keyNumbers.note: Research firm estimate, not a priced funding round. Treat as rough.

overview.whatItDoes: Midjourney makes images from text. You describe a scene, a style and a mood, and it draws it for you. It is known for images that look artistic and polished by default. It now also edits images and turns them into short video clips.
howItWorks: You write a prompt, which is a short text description, on the website or with the /imagine command in Discord.
Midjourney makes a grid of four options in a few seconds.
You upscale (make bigger and sharper) the one you like, or create variations of it.
You can add reference images to copy a style or a character's look.
Each plan gives a set number of fast GPU hours a month; Standard and higher also allow slower unlimited 'Relax' mode.
Images are public in a gallery by default, unless you pay for Pro or Mega to use Stealth mode.
overview.valueProposition: Beautiful, art-quality images from a sentence, cheaper and faster than hiring an artist for a rough idea.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Turns a prompt into four images. V8.1 became the default model in June 2026, making images in about 4 seconds.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The core reason people pay. Image quality is the product.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Make new versions of an image you like, or a bigger, sharper version.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Lets users steer toward what they want without writing better prompts.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Upload images to copy a style or a character's look. The V8.2 edit model takes up to four references.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Solves consistency, which professionals need for real projects.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Edit parts of an image and turn a still image into a short animated clip.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Keeps users from leaving for rival video tools.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Everyone can see others' images and prompts, and chat in Discord.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Free marketing and free teaching. New users learn by copying.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Keeps your images private. Only on Pro ($60) and Mega ($120).
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: A clear reason for professionals to pay more.

steps.detail: Finds a stunning Midjourney image on Instagram or Reddit.
Logs in and browses the Explore gallery.
Learns there is no free plan and picks Basic at $10.
Copies a prompt from the gallery and changes a few words.
Posts it online, which brings in the next user.
Client wants a cafe logo and interior mood board.
Uploads reference images for a warm, retro look.
Runs 20 to 30 prompts in an hour.
Uses variations and the editor to fix details.
Upgrades to Pro for Stealth mode.
Puts the best images in a deck for the client.

businessModel.summary: Midjourney makes money almost only from monthly subscriptions. There is no free plan and no ad money. A small licensing deal with Meta adds extra. The team is tiny, so most money left after GPU costs is profit.

revenueStreams.detail: $10 and $30 a month. Most of the paying base. Estimated about 70% of revenue.
$60 and $120 a month for heavy users and agencies. Estimated about 20% of revenue.
August 2025 deal giving Meta access to its image and video tech for undisclosed fees. Estimated about 10% with other income.

businessModel.pricing: Basic $10, Standard $30, Pro $60, Mega $120 per month. 20% off if paid yearly. No free trial since 2023.
costDrivers: GPUs (graphics chips) to train and run the models
A small team of about 40 people, mostly researchers and engineers
Legal costs from the Disney, Universal and artist lawsuits
Almost no marketing or sales spending
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a Standard user paying $30 a month. They get 15 fast GPU hours. Most people do not use all of them, and Relax mode runs when chips are free. If the real GPU cost is $8 to $12 for that user, Midjourney keeps about $18 to $22 before staff. Since it spends almost nothing on ads, CAC, the cost to get a new customer, is close to zero. That is why it is profitable with no investors.

howTheyGetUsers: People sharing images on social media, often with the Midjourney look people recognise
Discord server where anyone can watch others create
Public gallery that shows prompts, so new users see what is possible
Press coverage of viral AI images
whatBringsUsersBack: Monthly subscription with fast hours to use up
New model versions every few months
Ongoing projects that need more images
Community events and themes in Discord
growth.moat: Its moat is taste: its models make good-looking images with little effort, and its brand stands for quality. The community and years of user ratings help improve its models. But rivals like Google, OpenAI and open models are catching up fast, so the moat is thinner each year.

competitors.name: ChatGPT image generation (OpenAI)
competitors.positioning: Image making inside a chatbot millions already use, good at following instructions and text.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Midjourney is a dedicated art tool with a stronger artistic style and more controls.

competitors.name: Google Gemini image models (Nano Banana)
competitors.positioning: Fast image creation and editing inside Gemini, often free.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Midjourney charges for everything and wins on look, not price.

competitors.name: Adobe Firefly
competitors.positioning: AI images built into Photoshop, trained on licensed content for business safety.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Midjourney looks better to many users but carries more legal risk.

competitors.name: Stable Diffusion and Flux (open models)
competitors.positioning: Free models you can run yourself with full control.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Midjourney is easy and polished; open models need technical skill.

improvementIdeas.idea: Small free trial of 10 to 25 images on the website
improvementIdeas.problem: No free plan sends new users to free rivals
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More sign-ups that turn into paid plans

improvementIdeas.idea: Saved characters with a name you can reuse in any prompt
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More pro and storytelling use, higher retention
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of prompts using a saved character and churn of those users

improvementIdeas.idea: Team plan with shared billing, folders and private images
improvementIdeas.problem: Small teams and agencies have no clean way to pay and share
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher revenue per account and lower churn

improvementIdeas.problem: Legal risk for users and for Midjourney
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer risky images and a stronger legal position

pmLessons: A product that is clearly better can grow with zero marketing, because users share the output.
Charging from day one tells you fast if people value it. No free plan kept Midjourney profitable.
Start where your users already hang out. Launching in Discord gave Midjourney a community without building one.
Keep the team small and focused on the one thing that matters most, here image quality.
Legal risk over training data can become a product risk. Plan for it early.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Midjourney launch a free tier?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh more top-of-funnel users against GPU cost and brand. Suggest a small capped trial and measure trial to paid conversion and cost per new paid user.

interviewQuestions.question: Midjourney launched in Discord. Why, and was it a good choice?
interviewQuestions.hint: Talk about fast launch, built-in community, and public learning. Then the downsides: confusing for normal users, no control of the experience. Explain why a web app came later.

interviewQuestions.question: ChatGPT and Gemini now make images for free. How should Midjourney respond?
interviewQuestions.hint: Do not compete on price. Double down on quality, pro features like consistency and editing, and maybe team plans. Name metrics like churn and upgrade rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What north star metric would you pick for Midjourney?
interviewQuestions.hint: Images kept or downloaded per week. Explain why not images generated or revenue. Add guardrails like copyright flags and wait time.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design a video product for Midjourney?
interviewQuestions.hint: Start with users (designers, social creators), the job (short clips from images), costs (video uses far more GPU), and pricing by seconds of video.
